title: The Lifetime Achievement Award
clue: A gray muzzle, a lifetime of talents, and a ceremony in their honor.
reveal: Set up three gentle booths, one for each of your dog's lifelong talents. Your dog visits the one that calls to them, and the ceremony ends with a proper award and a citation read in your warmest voice.
objective: Offer low-impact versions of your dog's favorite old skills and honor the one they choose with a read-aloud citation.
instructions: List three things your dog has always loved: carrying things, finding things, digging, watching the street, tugging, sniffing. Choose three for your booths.

Build each as a low-effort booth on a non-slip mat at floor height. Carrier: a soft toy two steps away. Finder: three treats under a plain upside-down bowl. Digger: a folded towel with a treat tucked into a fold.
Set the three booths in a row and sit nearby. Invite your dog over once, and then wait.
Let them visit any booth, or none. Two minutes at a booth is a full shift.
Watch which one holds them longest. That is the winning talent.
Hold the ceremony: read the citation aloud in a warm voice ('For a lifetime of fine carrying'), and give a treat from the day's food.
Pack up the booths and give your dog a long rest.
twist: Your dog selects their own talent from three booths and receives a read-aloud award for it.
variations: One-booth version: honor a single talent.
Yard version: set the booths in a shady, level spot.
Watcher-only version: no booths, only a mat by the window and the citation.
Sunday version: pick a different booth each week.
completion: It counts once your dog has visited one booth and heard the citation. Resting through it is also fine.
photoIdea: Your dog at their chosen booth, in natural light, relaxed. No posing.
memoryPrompt: What talent won, and what did your dog do as a young dog that you will never forget?
substitutes: No towel? Use a folded blanket or a flat cushion.
dietNotes: Treats come from the day's ration. Ask your vet about your senior dog's diet.
safety: Keep every booth at floor height on a non-slip mat, with no jumping, climbing or steps.
Stop a booth if your dog tires, pants or limps, and follow your vet's advice on activity.
Take away anything your dog chews apart.
